newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing declines comment on new merger offer.
newsitem.headline: Boeing declines comment on new merger offer.

text.p: Boeing's European office declined to comment on Tuesday about reported last-minute proposals made to the European Commission to avert a ban of its proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
"We have no comment," Boeing's vice-president for European affairs Jim Frank said.

European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert told a scheduled meeting of EU foreign ministers that Boeing appeared to be easing its position on the controversial issue of exclusive supply pacts signed with three major U.S. airlines.
A diplomat said that Boeing sent the Commission a fax as Van Miert was having lunch with the ministers, the content of which was communicated to them.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Tuesday he hoped a deal would be reached on Wednesday, when the Commission must take a final decision.
Several EU foreign ministers including Germany's Klaus Kinkel and Britain's Robin Cook expressed similar hopes. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
